title: 2nd Mystery The Ease Of Essential Power

questions.question: How is Allah’s power described at the beginning of the passage in relation to light?
questions.answer: It is described as the purest and highest kind of light, above all other lights.

questions.question: How are the realities and inner aspects of created things portrayed?
questions.answer: They are portrayed as bright and reflective, like mirrors.

questions.question: Which created things are mentioned to show the full range of Allah’s creation?
questions.answer: The passage mentions atoms, plants, living creatures, stars, suns, and moons.

questions.question: What attitude do all created things have toward Allah’s command according to the passage?
questions.answer: They are fully obedient and submit to it.

questions.question: Why does the passage say creating countless things is as easy as creating one thing?
questions.answer: Because Allah’s power is absolute, luminous, and all things are under that power in complete obedience.

questions.question: What does the passage say about one task interfering with another?
questions.answer: It says that no task distracts from or blocks another.

questions.question: Which pairs of contrasts are said to be equal before Allah’s power?
questions.answer: Great and small, many and few, and particular and universal.

questions.question: What example is used to show how a very large object can be moved with ease?
questions.answer: A huge ship is compared to a toy being moved by a child’s finger.

questions.question: In the military example, what does one command show?
questions.answer: It shows that the same command can direct one soldier or a whole army.

questions.question: What is the point of the balance example with mountains and a walnut?
questions.answer: It shows that, under a wise law and proper balance, even something small can set very great things in motion.

questions.question: What qualities of Allah’s power are connected to order and balance in creation?
questions.answer: Divine justice and endless wisdom are connected to them.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is the source and foundation of order and regularity in creation?
questions.answer: Allah’s eternal power together with His justice and wisdom.

questions.question: How does the passage compare moving stars with moving atoms?
questions.answer: It says both are equally easy for Allah.

questions.question: What example from spring is used to compare giving life to one and to many?
questions.answer: Bringing one fly to life is compared with bringing the whole species of flies, along with many plants and animals, to life.

questions.question: What does the passage say happens to many living things in spring?
questions.answer: They are sent out onto the field of life through Allah’s wise and balanced power.

questions.question: How is reviving a tree in spring connected to reviving the earth?
questions.answer: The passage says both are done by the same wise and just power, with ease.

questions.question: What larger idea is supported by the image of the earth as a corpse in spring?
questions.answer: It supports the idea of resurrection on a vast scale.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying that hundreds of thousands of examples of resurrection appear in spring?
questions.answer: It means spring displays many signs of life returning after death, showing resurrection in countless forms.

questions.question: What central claim does the passage make about Allah’s power and difficulty?
questions.answer: Nothing is difficult for Allah’s power.

questions.question: Why are created things compared to mirrors in this passage?
questions.answer: Because their inner realities are presented as able to receive and display the effects of Divine power.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the relationship between creation and Allah’s command?
questions.answer: Creation responds in complete submission to Allah’s command.

questions.question: How does the passage connect obedience in creation with ease in creating many things?
questions.answer: Since creation obeys fully, producing many things together does not create any burden or conflict.

questions.question: What idea is emphasized by saying great and small are the same for Allah’s power?
questions.answer: Size does not make anything harder or easier for Allah.

questions.question: What is the lesson of the ship example?
questions.answer: A very large thing can be moved as easily as a very small toy when power acts through order.

questions.question: What human image is used to help explain commanding large numbers?
questions.answer: A ruler directing either one soldier or a whole army with one order.

questions.question: In the balance example, why is the walnut significant?
questions.answer: It shows that a small cause can trigger movement in very large masses when a precise system is in place.

questions.question: What does the balance example teach about Allah’s power?
questions.answer: It teaches that vast things can be directed with ease through wise laws.

questions.question: Which two Divine attributes are especially highlighted as shaping order in creation?
questions.answer: Justice and wisdom.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the link between Allah’s power and the regularity of the universe?
questions.answer: It says regularity and balance arise from Allah’s wise and just power.

questions.question: What does the passage imply by mentioning both stars and atoms together?
questions.answer: It implies that the biggest and smallest parts of creation are equally under Allah’s control.

questions.question: How does the spring example strengthen belief in Allah’s power over life?
questions.answer: It shows that giving life to one small creature and to entire groups of living things happens with the same ease.

questions.question: Besides flies, what other living beings are included in the spring revival?
questions.answer: Plants and animals are also included.

questions.question: How does the passage use the revival of a tree to help the reader understand a larger revival?
questions.answer: It uses the easier, familiar example of a tree coming to life to point to the earth’s broad renewal in spring.

questions.question: What is meant by calling the earth a corpse before spring revival?
questions.answer: It refers to the earth’s lifeless state in winter before new life appears.

questions.question: What overall conclusion about resurrection does the passage encourage the reader to draw from spring?
questions.answer: It encourages the reader to see spring as a clear sign that large-scale resurrection is easy for Allah.

questions.question: According to the passage, what makes Allah’s power unlike created power?
questions.answer: It is eternal, essential, luminous, and unlimited.

questions.question: How are all things said to stand before that power?
questions.answer: They stand in obedience and submission.

questions.question: What does the passage mean when it says countless things can be placed side by side easily?
questions.answer: It means Allah can create many things together without confusion, delay, or strain.

questions.question: What does the passage deny when it says no task interferes with another?
questions.answer: It denies that Allah’s attention or power is divided or overburdened by multiple acts.

questions.question: Why is the equality of many and few important in the passage?
questions.answer: It supports the idea that number does not limit Allah’s power.

questions.question: What example involving a child helps explain this idea?
questions.answer: A child moving a toy is used to compare with moving a huge ship.

questions.question: Why is the ship described as being as large as many houses?
questions.answer: To stress how enormous it is and make the ease of moving it more striking.

questions.question: What does the commander illustration add to the argument?
questions.answer: It shows that one command can direct either a single person or a whole group.

questions.question: What principle is being illustrated by the example of the balanced mountains?
questions.answer: That under an exact and wise system, a small addition can move very large things.

questions.question: What role does equilibrium play in the passage’s reasoning?
questions.answer: It shows that balance and order make action easy and effective.

questions.question: What does the passage identify as the beginning of order and regularity in creation?
questions.answer: Allah’s justice and endless wisdom within His eternal power.

questions.question: How does the passage connect universals and particulars to Allah’s command?
questions.answer: It says both the large-scale and the individual are equally obedient to that command.

questions.question: What does revolving the stars represent in the argument?
questions.answer: It represents one of the greatest visible actions in creation, yet still easy for Allah.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention reviving a single fly?
questions.answer: To give a small, familiar example of giving life.

questions.question: Why does it then mention reviving the whole species of flies and many other beings?
questions.answer: To show that multiplying the number does not increase difficulty for Allah.

questions.question: What similarity does the passage draw between reviving one tree and reviving the earth?
questions.answer: Both are carried out by the same just and wise power with full ease.

questions.question: What are the “different specimens of resurrection” in spring?
questions.answer: They are the many renewed forms of life that appear across the earth.

questions.question: What main belief does the whole passage aim to strengthen?
questions.answer: Trust in Allah’s unlimited power and certainty that resurrection is easy for Him.

questions.question: What image is used to describe Allah’s power before anything else in the passage?
questions.answer: The image of the finest and highest light.

questions.question: How does the passage portray the created world in relation to that power?
questions.answer: It portrays creation as reflective, receptive, and fully under Allah’s command.

questions.question: What range of creation is listed to show that everything is included?
questions.answer: The list runs from the tiniest particles and living things up to heavenly bodies.

questions.question: What does this broad range of examples suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests that nothing in existence falls outside Allah’s power.

questions.question: Why is it natural, according to the passage, that many things are made as easily as one?
questions.answer: Because Allah’s power is unlimited and creation is fully subject to it.

questions.question: What statement in the passage rejects the idea of competing tasks?
questions.answer: It says that one matter does not hold back another.

questions.question: How does the passage treat the difference between universal things and individual things?
questions.answer: It says that difference does not matter to Allah’s power.

questions.question: What does the giant ship example teach about scale?
questions.answer: It teaches that large scale does not create difficulty when power works through order.

questions.question: What does the child’s toy add to the ship comparison?
questions.answer: It makes the contrast vivid by putting extreme smallness next to extreme largeness.

questions.question: In the commander example, what remains the same whether one soldier or an army is sent?
questions.answer: The single order remains the same.

questions.question: What does that example imply about Divine command?
questions.answer: It implies that one command can govern many without any added difficulty.

questions.question: How does the balance example move the argument forward?
questions.answer: It shows that a tiny input can lead to major movement when a system is precisely arranged.

questions.question: Why are justice and wisdom important in the passage?
questions.answer: They explain how order, proportion, and balance exist throughout creation.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the obedience of all things to Allah’s power?
questions.answer: It says all things, whether small or great, follow His command and operation.

questions.question: How does the passage compare the movement of stars and atoms?
questions.answer: It says both are equally easy for Allah to move.

questions.question: What does spring demonstrate about Allah’s giving of life?
questions.answer: It demonstrates that bringing life to one creature and to entire groups happens with the same ease.

questions.question: How is the revival of the earth in spring described?
questions.answer: It is described as a resurrection of the earth’s lifeless body.

questions.question: What does this spring resurrection show about the greater resurrection?
questions.answer: It shows that raising vast numbers of beings is easy for Allah.

questions.question: What is the first reason given for the ease of creating countless things?
questions.answer: Allah’s power is presented as supremely subtle and luminous.

questions.question: What is the second reason tied to created things themselves?
questions.answer: Their realities are described as bright and mirror-like.

questions.question: What is the third reason connected to the behavior of creation?
questions.answer: All things are fully obedient to Allah’s command.

questions.question: What conclusion does the passage draw from these reasons?
questions.answer: That producing innumerable things together is completely easy for Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage say about overlap or conflict between Divine acts?
questions.answer: It says there is no interference between them.

questions.question: Which contrasts are used to show the complete reach of Allah’s power?
questions.answer: Large and small, many and few, and individual and universal.

questions.question: Why is the ship example effective for explaining the passage’s point?
questions.answer: It takes something extremely heavy and shows it being moved as simply as a toy.

questions.question: What deeper idea stands behind the ship example?
questions.answer: Order and control make what seems huge and difficult easy to direct.

questions.question: In the example of the commander, what does a single order prove?
questions.answer: It proves that command does not become harder when the number increases.

questions.question: Why does the passage use the image of a sensitive balance?
questions.answer: To illustrate how an exact system responds even to a small addition.

questions.question: What happens in the mountain example when a small object is added?
questions.answer: One side rises and the other falls, despite the huge masses involved.

questions.question: How is this example related to Divine power?
questions.answer: It suggests that Allah’s wise laws govern vast things with perfect ease.

questions.question: What is said to be at the root of all order and equilibrium in creation?
questions.answer: Divine justice and endless wisdom within Allah’s eternal power.

questions.question: How does the passage present stars and atoms as a comparison?
questions.answer: They are presented as equally manageable under Allah’s command.

questions.question: What does the passage teach through the example of the fly in spring?
questions.answer: That giving life to one small being is no harder for Allah than giving life to multitudes.

questions.question: What groups are revived along with the species of fly?
questions.answer: Many plants and animals are also revived.

questions.question: How does the passage connect a tree’s spring revival to a much larger event?
questions.answer: It uses the tree’s return to life as a sign of the earth’s broad renewal.

questions.question: What does the passage want the reader to recognize in the many spring renewals?
questions.answer: Signs of resurrection appearing in countless forms with complete ease.

questions.question: What picture of Allah’s power is given through the language of light?
questions.answer: It is pictured as the highest and purest light.

questions.question: How are the inner realities of created things described in relation to that light?
questions.answer: They are described as shining and able to reflect it like mirrors.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the response of all levels of creation to Allah’s power?
questions.answer: Every level of creation obeys and submits to it.

questions.question: How does that obedience help explain the ease of creation?
questions.answer: Because when all things submit fully, creating many at once involves no resistance or confusion.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the difference between one thing and countless things for Allah?
questions.answer: It says there is no real difference in difficulty.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the relation between separate Divine tasks?
questions.answer: They do not interrupt or hinder one another.

questions.question: What broad categories are all treated alike by Allah’s power?
questions.answer: The large and the small, the few and the many, and the individual and the general.

questions.question: What does the example of the huge ship and the child’s toy have in common?
questions.answer: Both are shown as movable with ease under proper power and order.

questions.question: Why does the commander example matter for understanding the passage?
questions.answer: It helps the reader see how one command can govern either one person or many.

questions.question: What does the image of two mountains on a balance emphasize?
questions.answer: It emphasizes precise equilibrium and the ease of affecting even huge masses within an ordered system.

questions.question: What role does the small walnut play in that example?
questions.answer: It shows that a tiny cause can trigger great effects.

questions.question: Which Divine qualities make order, regularity, and equilibrium possible?
questions.answer: Allah’s justice and never-ending wisdom.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the source of all created order?
questions.answer: It comes from Allah’s absolute and eternal power joined with wisdom and justice.

questions.question: How does the passage compare moving the stars with moving atoms?
questions.answer: It says both are equally easy for Allah.

questions.question: What is the significance of reviving one fly and all flies with the same command?
questions.answer: It shows that number does not increase the difficulty of giving life.

questions.question: What else is brought to life in spring besides flies?
questions.answer: Great hosts of plants and animals are also brought to life.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying Allah revives the corpse of the earth?
questions.answer: It means He restores life to the earth after its dead winter state.

questions.question: How does the passage use spring to teach about resurrection?
questions.answer: It presents spring as a recurring, visible example that mass resurrection is easy for Allah.
